steps.title: Triangles — rules to know
steps.intro: The general triangle rules. The angle sum and the exterior angle are the ones you will use most.

head: Rule
Statement
Remember
rows: vertex → midpoint of the opposite side
may fall outside an obtuse triangle
splits the angle at a vertex into two equal angles
no equal pieces, no right angle promised
\(=\) sum of the two interior angles not next to it
core rule — used again and again
the straight line is the shortest route
strict — never equal to either end

tips: Angle outside the triangle? Move it inside with vertical or adjacent angles first.
An expression of several angles? Write them all with ONE unknown — it usually cancels.

steps.stem: In triangle ABC, the marked angle outside the triangle and the interior angle at A are vertical angles. Based on this information and the information in the figure, what is the value of \(x\)?
explanation: The marked angle \(2x\) and the interior angle at A are vertical angles, therefore \(\angle A=2x\).
Angle sum: \(2x+3x+4x=180°\), that is \(9x=180°\). Therefore \(x=20°\).

\(q\) is an exterior angle at B. It equals the two interior angles not next to it: \(q=u+u=2u\).

steps.stem:
In triangle ABC:
\(\begin{cases} AC=7\text{ cm} \\ BC=12\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
Which of the following could be the length of AB (in cm)?
explanation: A side is between the difference and the sum of the other two sides: \(12-7<AB<12+7\), that is \(5<AB<19\).
Both signs are strict: \(5\) and \(19\) are not allowed, and \(21\) is too long. Only \(10\) fits.

steps.title: Special triangles
steps.intro: Isosceles means symmetric; equilateral means symmetric from every direction.

head: Triangle
Sides
Angles
Key fact
rows: to the base: median \(=\) altitude \(=\) bisector
every vertex line is a symmetry line

tips: Isosceles vertex angle \(v\): each base angle is \(\dfrac{180°-v}{2}\).
Several isosceles triangles share a vertex? Find the whole angle first, then subtract the part.
Two equal angles? Then the sides opposite them are equal — the triangle is isosceles.

steps.stem:
ABC is an equilateral triangle. Point D lies on BC.
Given:
\(\begin{cases} \angle DAC=30° \\ DC=6\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
What is AB (in cm)?
explanation: ABC is equilateral, therefore \(\angle BAC=60°\) and \(\angle BAD=60°-30°=30°\): AD bisects angle A.
In an equilateral triangle the angle bisector is also a median: \(BD=DC=6\).

In triangle ABC, point D lies on AB.
Given:
\(\begin{cases} AB=AC \\ \angle BAC=24° \\ BC=CD \end{cases}\)
What is \(\angle ACD\)?
explanation: ABC is isosceles: \(\angle B=\angle ACB=\frac{180°-24°}{2}=78°\).
BCD is isosceles (\(BC=CD\)): \(\angle BDC=\angle B=78°\), therefore \(\angle BCD=180°-78°-78°=24°\).

steps.stem: Points A and B lie on one line, and C, D and E lie on a parallel line. Given: \(DE=4CD\). What is \(\frac{\text{area of }BDE}{\text{area of }ACD}\)?
explanation: The lines are parallel, therefore both triangles have the same height \(h\).
Let \(CD=x\). Then \(DE=4x\).
\(\dfrac{S_{BDE}}{S_{ACD}}=\dfrac{\frac{4x\cdot h}{2}}{\frac{x\cdot h}{2}}=4\).
Without calculating: same height, therefore the area ratio is the base ratio, \(4\).

steps.stem:
Triangle ABC is right at C, and CD is the altitude to AB.
Given:
\(\begin{cases} AC=15\text{ cm} \\ BC=20\text{ cm} \\ AB=25\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
What is CD (in cm)?
explanation: Area with the legs: \(S=\frac{15\cdot20}{2}=150\).
Area with the side AB and its altitude CD: \(S=\frac{25\cdot CD}{2}\).
Same area: \(\frac{25\cdot CD}{2}=150\), therefore \(25\cdot CD=300\) and \(CD=12\).
Traps: \(6=150\div25\) forgets to double the area; \(12.5\) is half the hypotenuse (the median, not the altitude).

steps.stem:
In triangle ABC:
\(\begin{cases} AB=6\text{ cm} \\ BC=8\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
Which of the following could be the area of the triangle (in cm²)?
explanation: Take BC \(=8\) as the base. The height from A is a leg of a right triangle whose hypotenuse is AB \(=6\), therefore the height is at most \(6\).
Area \(\le\frac{8\cdot6}{2}=24\) (exactly \(24\) only when \(\angle B=90°\)).
\(25\), \(28\) and \(48\) are more than \(24\) — impossible. \(20\) is possible.
Trap: \(48=6\cdot8\) forgets to divide by \(2\).

steps.title: Triangle area — formulas
steps.intro: Area is a side times the altitude to that side, over 2 — any side, with its own height.

head: Shape
Area
Remember
rows: altitude outside? use only the side
same area from two sides — solve for the height
equal only with a right angle between them
vertex moves along a parallel line — the area does not change

tips: Triangles between parallel lines have the same height — the area ratio is the base ratio.
Two sides and no angle? The area can be anything up to half their product.

steps.title: The Pythagorean theorem
steps.intro: Right triangles only: the squares of the legs add up to the square of the hypotenuse.

head: Looking for
Do
Formula
rows: add the squares, then take the root
hypotenuse square minus leg square, then the root
compare the longest side squared with the other two squares

tips: Find the right-angle mark first; the hypotenuse is opposite it.
The hypotenuse is always the longest side — eliminate choices that are not longer than both legs.
A root answer is fine: \(\sqrt{65}\) is a finished length.

Triangle ABC is a right triangle.
Given:
\(\begin{cases} \angle ABC=90° \\ AB=8\text{ cm} \\ BC=15\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
What is AC (in cm)?
explanation: The right angle is at B, therefore AC is the hypotenuse — the longest side. \(8\) and \(15\) are out.
The trap \(23=8+15\) breaks the triangle rule: a side is less than the sum of the other two.

Given:
\(\begin{cases} \angle ABC=90° \\ AB=4\text{ cm} \\ BC=7\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)

Triangle ABC is a right triangle.
Given:
\(\begin{cases} \angle ABC=90° \\ AB=8\text{ cm} \\ AC=11\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
What is BC (in cm)?
explanation: The right angle is at B, therefore \(AC=11\) is the hypotenuse and BC is a leg.

steps.stem:
In triangle ABC:
\(\begin{cases} AB=6\text{ cm} \\ BC=7\text{ cm} \\ AC=10\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
Which of the following is true?
choices: The triangle is right, with the right angle at B.
The triangle is obtuse, with the obtuse angle at B.
The triangle is obtuse, with the obtuse angle at C.
explanation: The longest side is \(AC=10\): \(10^2=100\).
The other two sides: \(6^2+7^2=36+49=85\).
\(100>85\), therefore the angle opposite AC is obtuse. The angle opposite AC is the angle at B.

steps.title: Pythagorean triples
steps.intro: Whole-number right triangles — spot them and skip the calculation.
tips: The longest number is always the hypotenuse.
Multiply all three sides by the same factor — the ratio stays a right triangle.
5, 12, 13: a hamsa, a bat mitzvah, a bar mitzvah.

steps.stem: The accompanying figure shows three right triangles. The marked side lengths are in cm. What is CD (in cm)?
explanation: ABC: \(10=2\cdot5\) and \(26=2\cdot13\), the triple 5-12-13 times \(2\). Therefore \(AC=2\cdot12=24\).
ACE: legs \(18=6\cdot3\) and \(24=6\cdot4\), the triple 3-4-5 times \(6\). Therefore \(CE=6\cdot5=30\).
CED: two legs of \(30\). \(CD^2=30^2+30^2=2\cdot30^2\), therefore \(CD=30\sqrt2\).

steps.stem: ABC is an equilateral triangle with perimeter 18 cm. Points D and E are the midpoints of AB and BC, respectively. What is the area of quadrilateral ADEC (in cm²)?
explanation: Each side of ABC is \(18\div3=6\), therefore \(BD=BE=3\).

DBE has two sides of \(3\) with a \(60°\) angle between them. It is isosceles with a \(60°\) vertex angle, therefore its base angles are \(\frac{180°-60°}{2}=60°\) too: it is equilateral with side \(3\).
\(S_{ABC}=\frac{6^2\sqrt3}{4}=\frac{36\sqrt3}{4}\) and \(S_{DBE}=\frac{3^2\sqrt3}{4}=\frac{9\sqrt3}{4}\).
\(S_{ADEC}=\frac{36\sqrt3}{4}-\frac{9\sqrt3}{4}=\frac{27\sqrt3}{4}\).

steps.title: Special right triangles
steps.intro: One side is enough to find the other two.

head: Triangle
Sides
Moves
rows: short leg \(\times2\) = hypotenuse · short \(\times\sqrt3\) = long · long \(\div\sqrt3\) = short
altitude = \(\frac a2\) — two golden triangles back to back · area = \(\frac{a^2\sqrt3}{4}\)

tips: Short leg is opposite \(30°\), long leg opposite \(60°\) — double only the short leg.
Dividing by a root: ignore the root, divide, attach it back — \(\frac{9}{\sqrt3}=3\sqrt3\), \(\frac{14}{\sqrt2}=7\sqrt2\).
Subtracting equilateral areas? Keep the denominator 4 until the end.

steps.stem:
Triangle ABC is a right triangle.
Given:
\(\begin{cases} \angle ABC=90° \\ \angle ACB=45° \\ AC=14\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
What is its perimeter (in cm)?
explanation: \(\angle C=45°\), therefore \(\angle A=45°\) too: a 45°-45°-90° triangle with hypotenuse \(AC=14\).
Each leg: \(\frac{14}{\sqrt2}=7\sqrt2\).
Perimeter \(=7\sqrt2+7\sqrt2+14=14+14\sqrt2\).

explanation: The third side is between the difference and the sum: \(11-8<x<11+8\), that is \(3<x<19\).
\(3\) is not allowed (strict sign). \(7\), \(12\) and \(18\) are all inside.

explanation: A median splits a triangle into two triangles of equal area: \(S_{ACD}=\frac{30}{2}=15\).

explanation: The median bisects the base, and the two small triangles share the same height, therefore their areas are equal.
The original triangle: \(19+19=38\).

In a right triangle, one acute angle is x. The other is divided into five equal angles, each measuring x. What is x?
explanation: The two acute angles of a right triangle add up to \(90°\). Together they are \(1+5=6\) angles of \(x\).

steps.stem: In a right triangle, one acute angle is \(2\alpha\). What is the exterior angle adjacent to the other acute angle?
explanation: The angles of the triangle: \(90°\), \(2\alpha\) and the other acute angle.
The exterior angle next to the other acute angle equals the two interior angles not next to it: \(90°+2\alpha\).

steps.stem: ABC is isosceles, with \(AC=BC\). Based on this information and the information in the figure, what is the value of \(x\)?
explanation: The interior angle at A is adjacent to \(146°\): \(\angle A=180°-146°=34°\).
\(AC=BC\), therefore the angles opposite them are equal: \(\angle B=\angle A=34°\).

Which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: Angle A is the largest angle
explanation: The third side is between the difference and the sum: \(26-19<BC<26+19\), that is \(7<BC<45\).
Therefore \(BC>7\) is always true.
BC can be less than \(19\) or more than \(26\), therefore choices 1 and 2 are not necessarily true. Angle A is opposite BC, and BC need not be the longest side.

steps.stem: The exterior angles adjacent to the interior angles at P and Q of triangle PQR are u and v, respectively. Given: u>v. Which of the following is necessarily true?
explanation: \(\angle P=180°-u\) and \(\angle Q=180°-v\). Since \(u>v\): \(\angle P<\angle Q\).
The side opposite P is QR, and the side opposite Q is PR. The smaller angle is opposite the shorter side: \(QR<PR\).

steps.stem: A triangle has two sides of lengths 9 cm and 14 cm. If the third side has an integer length, how many different lengths are possible?
explanation: Whole numbers from \(6\) to \(22\): \(22-6+1=17\).
Shortcut: twice the shorter side, minus 1: \(2\cdot9-1=17\).

steps.stem: Two sides of a triangle are 10 cm and 7 cm long. What is the largest possible area of the triangle (in cm²)?
explanation: Put the side \(10\) on the floor. The height is at most \(7\) (the side \(7\) standing straight up).
Largest area \(=\frac{10\cdot7}{2}=35\), with a right angle between the two sides.
Trap: \(70=10\cdot7\) forgets to divide by \(2\).

steps.stem: In the accompanying figure, the two horizontal lines are parallel and \(AB=BC\). What is the value of \(y\)?
explanation: \(AB=BC\), therefore \(\angle A=\angle C=\frac{180°-42°}{2}=69°\).
Alternate angles between the parallel lines: \(y=\angle C=69°\).

steps.stem: In the accompanying figure, line \(\ell\) is parallel to BC. The extension of side AC meets \(\ell\) at E. Which expression equals \(r\)?
explanation: The interior angle at B is adjacent to \(q\): \(\angle B=180°-q\).
The exterior angle at C equals the two interior angles not next to it: \(p+(180°-q)\).
\(\ell\parallel BC\), therefore \(r\) equals this exterior angle (corresponding angles): \(r=180°-q+p\).
Check with numbers: \(p=70°\) and \(q=120°\) give \(\angle B=60°\) and \(\angle C=50°\). The exterior angle at C is \(130°=180°-120°+70°\) ✓.

Triangle ADC is equilateral, and B, D and C lie on one line in that order.
Given:
\(\begin{cases} BD=7\text{ cm} \\ \angle BAD=30° \end{cases}\)
What is DC (in cm)?
explanation: \(\angle ADC=60°\) (equilateral). It is an exterior angle of ABD: \(60°=30°+\angle ABD\), therefore \(\angle ABD=30°\).
Two equal angles (\(30°\) at A and at B), therefore the sides opposite them are equal: \(AD=BD=7\).
ADC is equilateral, therefore \(DC=AD=7\).

steps.stem: Which of the following could be the side lengths of an acute triangle (in cm)?
explanation: Compare the longest side squared with the sum of the other two squares.
\(2, 3, 6\): \(2+3<6\) — not a triangle at all.

steps.stem: An equilateral triangle has area \(25\sqrt3\) cm². What is its perimeter (in cm)?
explanation: \(\frac{a^2\sqrt3}{4}=25\sqrt3\), therefore \(a^2=100\) and \(a=10\).
Perimeter \(=3\cdot10=30\).

steps.stem: In the accompanying figure, \(DE\parallel AC\) and \(BD=6\) cm. What is the area of triangle BDE (in cm²)?
explanation: The angles next to the two marked \(120°\) angles are \(180°-120°=60°\): \(\angle BDE=60°\) and \(\angle ACB=60°\).
\(DE\parallel AC\), therefore \(\angle DEB=\angle ACB=60°\) (corresponding angles). BDE has two \(60°\) angles, therefore it is equilateral with side \(6\).
Area \(=\frac{6^2\sqrt3}{4}=\frac{36\sqrt3}{4}=9\sqrt3\).

In triangle ABC:
\(\begin{cases} AB=AC=10\text{ cm} \\ \angle BAC=120° \end{cases}\)
What is the area of the triangle (in cm²)?
explanation: The base angles: \(\frac{180°-120°}{2}=30°\). The altitude from A cuts the triangle into two 30°-60°-90° triangles with hypotenuse \(10\).
Height (opposite \(30°\)) \(=\frac{10}{2}=5\). Half the base \(=5\sqrt3\), therefore \(BC=10\sqrt3\).
Area \(=\frac{10\sqrt3\cdot5}{2}=25\sqrt3\) — the same as \(\frac{a^2\sqrt3}{4}\) with \(a=10\).

steps.stem: A right isosceles triangle has perimeter \(16+8\sqrt2\) cm. What is its area (in cm²)?
explanation: Each leg is \(t\) and the hypotenuse is \(t\sqrt2\): \(P=2t+t\sqrt2=t(2+\sqrt2)\).
\(16+8\sqrt2=8(2+\sqrt2)\), therefore \(t=8\).
Area \(=\frac{8\cdot8}{2}=32\).

steps.stem: ABC is an obtuse triangle, with \(\angle ACB>90°\) and \(AB=6\) cm. Which of the following could be its perimeter (in cm)?
explanation: Minimum: \(AC+BC>AB=6\), therefore the perimeter is more than \(6+6=12\).
Maximum: \(\angle C>90°\) is the largest angle, therefore AB is the longest side: \(AC<6\) and \(BC<6\). The perimeter is less than \(6+6+6=18\).
Only \(13.5\) is between \(12\) and \(18\).
Example: sides \(3.75,\ 3.75,\ 6\). The obtuse test: \(6^2=36>3.75^2+3.75^2=28.125\), therefore the angle opposite AB is obtuse.

steps.stem: Which of the following triangles is not necessarily isosceles?
choices: A triangle with a median of length 6 cm drawn to a side of length 4 cm
A triangle in which an altitude also bisects the angle at its starting vertex
A triangle in which a median is perpendicular to the side it meets
explanation: Choice 2: the third angle is \(180°-76°-52°=52°\). Two equal angles, therefore two equal sides: isosceles.
Choice 3: an altitude that also bisects its angle is a symmetry line: isosceles.
Choice 4: a median that is perpendicular to its side is a symmetry line: isosceles.
Choice 1: a median of \(6\) to a side of \(4\) can lean to one side. Then the other two sides are different: not necessarily isosceles.

ACD: leg \(10\) and hypotenuse \(26\), the triple 5-12-13 times \(2\). Therefore \(CD=24\).

In triangle ABC, AE is the altitude to BC. Point D lies on AE, and DBC is an equilateral triangle.
Given:
\(\begin{cases} BE=3\text{ cm} \\ AD=2\sqrt3\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
What is the shaded area (in cm²)?
explanation: DE is the altitude of the equilateral triangle DBC, therefore it is also a median: \(EC=BE=3\) and \(BC=6\).
DEC is a 30°-60°-90° triangle with short leg \(EC=3\): \(DE=3\sqrt3\). Therefore \(AE=3\sqrt3+2\sqrt3=5\sqrt3\).

Shaded area \(=15\sqrt3-9\sqrt3=6\sqrt3\).

steps.stem: Triangle ABC has area 32 cm². Point D lies on BC, and \(DC=3BD\). What is the difference between the areas of ADC and ABD (in cm²)?
explanation: ABD and ADC have the same height from A. Therefore their areas are in the ratio of their bases, 1 to 3.
Four equal parts: \(32\div4=8\). \(S_{ABD}=8\) and \(S_{ADC}=3\cdot8=24\).
Difference: \(24-8=16\).

steps.stem: Four congruent squares, each with side 3 cm, are arranged as in the accompanying figure. What is the perimeter of AEF minus the perimeter of AFG (in cm)?
explanation: AE is made of two diagonals of small squares: \(AE=3\sqrt2+3\sqrt2=6\sqrt2\). \(AG=3+3=6\).
AF is in both triangles, and \(EF=FG=3\). These cancel in the difference.
\(P_{AEF}-P_{AFG}=AE-AG=6\sqrt2-6\).
Full calculation: \(AF=\sqrt{6^2+3^2}=\sqrt{45}=3\sqrt5\), \(P_{AEF}=6\sqrt2+3+3\sqrt5\), \(P_{AFG}=6+3+3\sqrt5\).

steps.stem: The accompanying figure shows two equilateral triangles with side lengths a and b, where \(a<b\). The total length of the bold segments is twice the perimeter of the smaller triangle. What is \(\frac ab\)?
explanation: The bold line: \(b+b+(b-a)=3b-a\).
Twice the small perimeter: \(2\cdot3a=6a\).
\(3b-a=6a\), therefore \(3b=7a\) and \(\frac ab=\frac37\).

steps.stem: In an isosceles triangle, each equal side is four times as long as the base. What is the ratio of the perimeter to the length of an equal side?
explanation: Let the base be \(1\). Each equal side is \(4\), and the perimeter is \(1+4+4=9\).
\(\frac{\text{perimeter}}{\text{equal side}}=\frac94\).

steps.stem: The shortest and longest sides of a triangle are 2 cm and 7 cm, respectively. Which of the following could be the length of its third side (in cm)?
explanation: \(7\) is the longest side, therefore \(x<7\).
Triangle rule: \(2+x>7\), therefore \(x>5\).
Only \(6.5\) is between \(5\) and \(7\).

steps.stem: Two triangles share a base of length 14 cm. Their third vertices lie on opposite sides of the base line, at perpendicular distances of 5 cm and 9 cm from it. What is the area of the figure formed by their union (in cm²)?
explanation: The triangles are on opposite sides of the base, therefore they do not overlap.
Or at once: \(\frac{14\cdot(5+9)}{2}=98\).

steps.stem: In triangle ABC, angle B is 35° and angle A is greater than 45°. BC is extended beyond C to D. Which of the following cannot be the measure of angle ACD?
explanation: Angle ACD is an exterior angle of the triangle: \(\angle ACD=\angle A+35°\).
\(\angle A>45°\), therefore \(\angle ACD>80°\). \(75°\) is impossible.
The other choices work: \(95°\), \(115°\) and \(135°\) give \(\angle A=60°\), \(80°\) and \(100°\).

steps.stem: Which of the following is necessarily true for every isosceles triangle?
choices: Each equal side is longer than the base
Every altitude is also an angle bisector
The altitude to the base is shorter than an equal side
explanation: The altitude to the base makes two right triangles. In each one, an equal side is the hypotenuse and the altitude is a leg. The hypotenuse is the longest side, therefore the altitude is shorter than an equal side.
The others are not always true. Sides \(5,\ 5,\ 8\): the equal sides are shorter than the base, and the triangle is obtuse (\(8^2=64>5^2+5^2=50\)). Only the altitude to the base is also a bisector.

steps.stem: Which of the following triangles is not necessarily equilateral?
choices: A triangle in which an altitude also bisects the angle at its starting vertex
A triangle with two angles of \(60°\)
An isosceles triangle with one angle of \(60°\)
An isosceles triangle whose base is twice half of an equal side
explanation: An altitude that also bisects its starting angle makes the triangle isosceles. It does not force the base to equal the other two sides.
Example: a triangle with sides \(5,\ 5,\ 6\) has this symmetry line, but it is not equilateral.

steps.stem: One triangle has angles \(2p\), \(q\) and 42°. Another has angles \(p\), \(2q\) and 66°. What is \(p+q\)?
explanation: Angle sums: \(\begin{cases} 2p+q+42°=180° \\ p+2q+66°=180° \end{cases}\), that is \(\begin{cases} 2p+q=138° \\ p+2q=114° \end{cases}\)
Add the two equations: \(3p+3q=252°\), therefore \(p+q=84°\).

steps.stem: A, C and B lie on one line. CE bisects angle ACD, and CF bisects angle DCB. E and F lie on these bisectors. Given: angle CEF is \(2t\). Which expression equals angle EFC?
explanation: \(\angle ACD+\angle DCB=180°\). Their halves: \(\angle ECD+\angle DCF=90°\), therefore \(\angle ECF=90°\).
Triangle ECF: \(\angle EFC=180°-90°-2t=90°-2t\).

steps.stem: In the accompanying figure, ABC is a right isosceles triangle with \(AB=BC=4\) cm, and ACD is equilateral. What is the perimeter of quadrilateral ABCD (in cm)?
explanation: ABC: legs \(4\) and \(4\), therefore \(AC=4\sqrt2\).
ACD is equilateral: \(AD=CD=AC=4\sqrt2\).
Perimeter (outside sides only): \(4+4+4\sqrt2+4\sqrt2=8+8\sqrt2\). AC is inside and is not counted.

steps.stem: The angles of a triangle are \(2x\), \(4x\) and \(6x\). Which of the following could be its side lengths (in cm)?
explanation: A 30°-60°-90° triangle has sides \(a,\ a\sqrt3,\ 2a\). With \(a=5\): \(5,\ 5\sqrt3,\ 10\).

steps.stem: Which of the following triangles is not necessarily equilateral?
choices: A triangle with two angles of \(60°\)
A triangle in which one median is also an altitude
An isosceles triangle with one angle of \(60°\)
A triangle in which two different medians are also altitudes
explanation: Choice 1: the third angle is \(180°-60°-60°=60°\): equilateral.
Choice 3: a \(60°\) vertex angle gives base angles of \(\frac{180°-60°}{2}=60°\); \(60°\) base angles give a third angle of \(60°\): equilateral.
Choice 4: each such median is a symmetry line, therefore two pairs of sides are equal: all three sides are equal.
Choice 2: one symmetry line makes the triangle only isosceles. Example: sides \(5,\ 5,\ 6\) — not equilateral.

steps.stem: A triangle has side lengths 10 cm, 10 cm and 12 cm. What is its area (in cm²)?
explanation: The altitude to the base is also a median: it cuts the base \(12\) into \(6\) and \(6\).
Each half is a right triangle with hypotenuse \(10\) and leg \(6\) (the triple 3-4-5 times \(2\)), therefore the altitude is \(8\).

steps.stem: AD is an altitude in triangle ABC, with D on BC. Given: \(BD=\frac34BC\). The area of ADC is 14 cm². What is the area of ABD (in cm²)?
explanation: \(BD=\frac34BC\), therefore \(DC=\frac14BC\) and \(BD=3\cdot DC\).
ABD and ADC have the same height AD. Therefore \(S_{ABD}=3\cdot S_{ADC}=3\cdot14=42\).

Triangle ABC is right at C, and D is the midpoint of BC.
Given:
\(\begin{cases} AC=12\text{ cm} \\ BC=16\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
Which statement compares triangles ADC and ADB correctly?
choices: Their areas are equal, and ADC has the smaller perimeter
Their areas and perimeters are equal
ADC has the smaller area and the smaller perimeter
Their areas are equal, and ADB has the smaller perimeter
explanation: AD is a median, therefore \(S_{ADC}=S_{ADB}\).
Perimeters: both have AD, and \(DC=DB=8\). Only AC and AB are different.
\(AB=20\) (the triple 3-4-5 times \(4\)) and \(AC=12\). Therefore ADC has the smaller perimeter.

Triangles ABC and ACD are right at B and at C, respectively, and they have equal areas.
Given:
\(\begin{cases} AB=9\text{ cm} \\ BC=12\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
What is CD (in cm)?
explanation: ABC: \(9=3\cdot3\) and \(12=3\cdot4\), the triple 3-4-5 times \(3\). Therefore \(AC=15\).
ACD is right at C, with legs AC and CD: \(\frac{15\cdot CD}{2}=54\), therefore \(CD=\frac{108}{15}=\frac{36}{5}\).

steps.stem: Two sides of a triangle are 12 cm and 9 cm long. The altitude to the 12 cm side is 6 cm. What is the altitude to the 9 cm side (in cm)?
explanation: Area with the side \(12\): \(\frac{12\cdot6}{2}=36\).
Area with the side \(9\) and its altitude \(h\): \(\frac{9h}{2}=36\), therefore \(9h=72\) and \(h=8\).
Sense check: the shorter side has the longer altitude. Trap: \(4.5=\frac{9\cdot6}{12}\) turns the ratio upside down.

steps.stem:
Triangle ABC is right at A, and AD is the altitude to BC.
Given:
\(\begin{cases} AB=8\text{ cm} \\ AC=15\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
What is AD (in cm)?
explanation: Area two ways: \(\frac{8\cdot15}{2}=\frac{17\cdot AD}{2}\), therefore \(17\cdot AD=120\) and \(AD=\frac{120}{17}\).

steps.stem:
In triangle ABC, BD bisects angle B and meets AC at D.
Given:
\(\begin{cases} AB=AC \\ AD=DB \end{cases}\)
What is angle B?
explanation: Let each half of angle B be \(x\): \(\angle ABD=\angle DBC=x\).
\(AD=DB\), therefore \(\angle A=\angle ABD=x\).
\(AB=AC\), therefore \(\angle C=\angle B=2x\).
Angle sum: \(x+2x+2x=180°\), therefore \(x=36°\) and \(\angle B=72°\).

steps.stem: At each vertex of a triangle, take the reflex angle outside the triangle (the reflex angle \(=360°\) minus the interior angle). What is the average of these three reflex angles?
explanation: Plug in: an equilateral triangle gives \(360°-60°=300°\) at each vertex.

steps.stem: Two angles of a triangle are \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\). At the third vertex, the reflex angle outside the triangle (the reflex angle \(=360°\) minus the interior angle) is divided into three equal angles, each measuring \(\delta\). Which expression equals \(\delta\)?
explanation: The third angle: \(180°-\alpha-\beta\).
The reflex angle: \(360°-(180°-\alpha-\beta)=180°+\alpha+\beta\).
\(\delta=\frac{180°+\alpha+\beta}{3}=60°+\frac{\alpha+\beta}{3}\).

steps.stem:
In the accompanying figure, AD bisects angle BAC.
Given:
\(\begin{cases} AC=BC \\ AB\parallel CD \\ \angle ACB=2t \end{cases}\)
Which expression equals x?
explanation: \(AC=BC\), therefore \(\angle BAC=\angle ABC=\frac{180°-2t}{2}=90°-t\).
AD bisects angle A: \(\angle BAD=\frac{90°-t}{2}=45°-\frac t2\).
Alternate angles (\(AB\parallel CD\)): \(x=\angle BAD=45°-\frac t2\).

A, E and B lie on one line in that order; D, E and C lie on another. The marked angles at A and C are right angles.
Given:
\(\begin{cases} BC=2 \\ CE=2\sqrt3 \\ AD=4\sqrt3 \end{cases}\)
What is AB?
explanation: EBC is right at C, with legs \(BC=2\) and \(CE=2\sqrt3\): the ratio \(a,\ a\sqrt3\) with \(a=2\). It is a 30°-60°-90° triangle: \(EB=2\cdot2=4\), and \(\angle BEC=30°\) (opposite the short leg BC).
Vertical angles: \(\angle AED=30°\).
AED is right at A. \(AD=4\sqrt3\) is opposite the \(30°\) angle, therefore it is the short leg. The long leg: \(AE=4\sqrt3\cdot\sqrt3=12\).

steps.stem: In a 30°–60°–90° triangle, the difference between the hypotenuse and the shorter leg is 7 cm. What is the area (in cm²)?
explanation: Sides \(a,\ a\sqrt3,\ 2a\). The hypotenuse minus the short leg: \(2a-a=a\), therefore \(a=7\).
Legs \(7\) and \(7\sqrt3\). Area \(=\frac{7\cdot7\sqrt3}{2}=\frac{49\sqrt3}{2}\).

steps.stem: The side opposite an obtuse angle of a triangle is 8 cm long. Which of the following could be the sum of the other two side lengths (in cm)?
explanation: Triangle rule: the other two sides together are more than \(8\).
The obtuse angle is the largest angle, therefore \(8\) is the longest side. Each other side is less than \(8\), and their sum is less than \(16\).

steps.stem:
In triangle ABC, angle B is obtuse.
Given:
\(\begin{cases} AB=8\text{ cm} \\ BC=15\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
Which of the following could be AC (in cm)?
explanation: Angle B is obtuse, therefore AC (opposite B) satisfies \(AC^2>8^2+15^2=289\), that is \(AC>17\).
Triangle rule: \(AC<8+15=23\).
Only \(20\) is between \(17\) and \(23\). (\(17\) gives a right angle at B.)

steps.stem: The area of triangle ABC is 18 cm², and \(AB=4\) cm. Which of the following could be the length of BC (in cm)?
explanation: Take AB as the base. The height from C is at most BC.
Therefore \(18\le\frac{4\cdot BC}{2}=2\cdot BC\), that is \(BC\ge9\).
Only \(10\) is at least \(9\).

steps.stem:
In triangle ABC:
\(\begin{cases} AB=5\text{ cm} \\ AC=8\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
The area of the triangle is 20 cm². What is angle A?
explanation: The largest possible area with sides \(5\) and \(8\) is \(\frac{5\cdot8}{2}=20\).
The area is exactly \(20\), the largest possible. This happens only when the two sides are perpendicular: \(\angle A=90°\).

steps.stem: A triangle has integer side lengths. Two sides are 6 cm and 10 cm. How many possible third-side lengths make the 10 cm side the unique longest side?
explanation: Triangle rule: \(10-6<x<10+6\), that is \(4<x<16\).
\(10\) must be the only longest side: \(x<10\).
Whole numbers: \(5, 6, 7, 8, 9\) — five values.

steps.stem: Two sides of a triangle are 8 cm and 13 cm long. The third side has a whole-number length, and the triangle is obtuse. How many different lengths are possible for the third side?
explanation: Triangle rule: \(13-8<x<13+8\), that is \(5<x<21\): the whole numbers \(6\) to \(20\).
If \(x\) is the longest side: \(x^2>8^2+13^2=233\). \(15^2=225\) is too small and \(16^2=256\) works: \(x=16\) to \(20\), five lengths.
If \(13\) is the longest side: \(13^2=169>64+x^2\), that is \(x^2<105\): \(x=6\) to \(10\), five lengths.
Total: \(5+5=10\). (\(x=11\) to \(15\) give acute triangles.)

steps.stem: In triangle ABC, D lies on BC, and the ratio \(BD:DC\) is \(2:5\). E is the midpoint of AD. What is the ratio of the area of EBD to the area of ABC?
explanation: ABD and ABC have the same height from A: \(\frac{S_{ABD}}{S_{ABC}}=\frac{BD}{BC}=\frac27\).
E is the midpoint of AD, therefore E is half as high above BC as A: \(S_{EBD}=\frac12S_{ABD}=\frac12\cdot\frac27S_{ABC}=\frac17S_{ABC}\).

steps.stem: A right triangle has perimeter 60 cm and hypotenuse 26 cm. What is its area (in cm²)?
explanation: Algebra: \((a+b)^2=a^2+2ab+b^2\): \(34^2=1156=676+2ab\), therefore \(2ab=480\) and the area is \(\frac{ab}{2}=120\).

steps.stem: An equilateral triangle and a right isosceles triangle have equal perimeters. Each side of the equilateral triangle is 8 cm. What is a leg of the right isosceles triangle (in cm)?
explanation: The common perimeter: \(3\cdot8=24\). With leg \(x\), the hypotenuse is \(x\sqrt2\): \(x(2+\sqrt2)=24\).
Work back from the choices: \(12(2-\sqrt2)\cdot(2+\sqrt2)=12(4-2)=24\) ✓.
